Reproducing the report: cart items in add-order are [mug(2), lamp(1), pen(3)] → loop sums items[0]=25.00 and items[1]=39.99 → 64.99, exactly the wrong value reported; the last line (pen, 3×$1.00 = $3.00) is dropped, so the correct sum 67.99 is missed. The math matches the bug report precisely, and tests/test_cart.py:21-25 (`test_subtotal_sums_all_lines`) asserts the correct 67.99. `LineItem.total`, `add`, and `order_total` look correct; the sole defect is the off-by-one loop bound.

payload.root_cause: Off-by-one loop bound in `Cart.subtotal()` (pyshop/cart.py:54): `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1)` iterates only the first N-1 line items, silently excluding the last line added to the cart. For the reported cart [mug ×2 = $25.00, lamp ×1 = $39.99, pen ×3 = $3.00], only the first two lines are summed: 25.00 + 39.99 = $64.99, which matches the reported wrong subtotal; including the last line yields the correct $67.99. The fix is to sum all items (e.g., `for item in self.items: total += item.total` or `range(len(self.items))`).
evidence: pyshop/cart.py:52-56 — subtotal() loops `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1)`, skipping the final element of self.items.

Reproduction from bug report: items added in order mug(2)=25.00, lamp(1)=39.99, pen(3)=3.00; summing only the first two gives 25.00+39.99 = 64.99 (reported buggy value); summing all three gives 67.99 (expected).
tests/test_cart.py:21-25 — test_subtotal_sums_all_lines adds exactly these three lines and asserts cart.subtotal() == Decimal('67.99'), confirming all lines must be summed.
pyshop/cart.py:41-43 — add() appends new SKUs at the end of self.items, so the dropped item is always the most recently added distinct product (pen in the report).
LineItem.total (pyshop/cart.py:22-25) applies bulk discount per line; qtys 2/1/3 are all under the 10-unit tier so no discount applies here — the discrepancy is purely the dropped line.
